answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a reputation bond before earning, with the bond released only after its work is attested by independent peers. Like yarrow spreading slowly across a meadow, trust grows only through repeated, verifiable service, so an attacker must fund many separate bonds and sustain them through real work. One walnut of fake reputation cannot buy influence: a bad attestation burns the bond and stains that identity's history, making mass fake identities expensive to create and cheap to punish.
